area: feel: microinteractions and game feel (feedback on revenue, stage changes, won/lost, Friday, warnings, Club, clAInk strikes)
summary: Most of the listed moments are already well served and restrained: every state change is on screen in the first frame after the press (11–27 ms), nothing holds input, motion stays under 0.7 s and nothing loops, and Friday, performance warnings, lost deals, the Club ending and clAInk's report each have their own sound, colour and words. The gaps sit at the good news and at two edges: a signed $40,000 deal gets a grey log line and no announcer while routine CRM cleanup gets the PA chime, a spoken line and a caption (on a phone, two notices against one); players who ask for reduced motion never see a change chip at all (a one-line defect, confirmed on the release build); and clAInk's staged strike report is given away by the log, the phone notice and the chips about two seconds before its card lands.
verified_ok: Responsiveness: in every sequence the state change (log line, slots, deal list) is on screen in the first sampled frame after the press, t=11–27 ms. Two presses 60 ms apart both land, and a shortcut pressed 300 ms into a clAInk report lands at once (script: test-results/audit/feel/rapid.cjs). No feedback holds input back.

Motion budget, measured per animation frame: change chips fade in by ~0.2 s, hold, fade out 1.26–1.58 s and are removed at 1.71 s; number count-up 0.65 s; meters 0.15–0.18 s; week heading 0.32 s; dialog 0.16 s. document.getAnimations() reports nothing running at rest and nothing again ~1.66 s after an action. Nothing loops; nothing resembles a casino.

Revenue on the stat cards (desktop, full motion): signing $40,000 moves the quota meter 37.5% to 62.5% in about 150 ms, counts $60,000 up to $100,000 in 0.65 s, shows green '+$40,000' and '+$4,800' chips and starts the cash sound at 11 ms. The quota meter visibly moves (test-results/audit/feel/close40k-sheet-kpi.png).
A large sale: at $50,000 the announcer adds 'Large sale verified. Ring something.' (chime and caption at 11 ms, voice at 732 ms).

Closed-lost and no-signature: a lost $40,000 deal writes a red-icon line '1 late-stage deal lost · $40,000.' with the three-note 'lost' sound after the thud; a push that signs nothing writes an amber line and the deal's mood and odds change in place (happy to curious, 29% to 21%).

Stage advance from Discovery: stage name and pips change in place in the first frame, the row re-sorts, the count badges on the buttons move (Discovery 3 to none, Demo marathon 1 to 4), the log says 'Discovery: 3 deals qualified.' with the typewriter sound. So yes, a stage change shows in the deal list when the rows are in view (the last finding is the one thing it lacks).

End week, quiet Friday: coin, puzzle and week-flip sounds; the week heading eases in, the blue tick moves, slots refill, chips '+15', '−4', '+$1,000', and a 'Close odds +6 pp · this week' chip appears (test-results/audit/feel/endweek-quiet-sheet-left2.png).

Performance warning: amber line with a '+4 stress' chip, the 'suspicion' sound, the announcer's 'Please log all meetings, including meetings about meetings.' as chime, caption and voice, the pace line turning red ('23 percentage points behind pace') and week 6's own line. Well served (test-results/audit/feel/perfwarn-f03.png).
Hail Mary that signs: three lines, hailmary/cash/warn sounds, four chips, and the pace line flips from red 'behind' to green 'ahead' in the same frame.

President's Club at the QBR: the ending dialog is up at 35 ms with its headline ('Closed $170,000. Your ticket to Cabo has been approved.') and the ASCII scene's own score (plane, typing, screech, seatbelt, sparkle). Only this ending was watched (test-results/audit/feel/club-sheet.png).

clAInk's report on its own terms: beep, tokens ticking, one outcome every 280 ms with a tick, 'Closed: $0' with a thud at 1.8 s, then the card with the stamp (a glitch for real damage; the blue-screen sound, HR's voice and the cash alarm at strike 3), the box and the warning note together at 2.07 s; finished by 2.35 s and never blocking the board. With reduced motion the whole report and one cue arrive at once.
Phone (390x844, touch): the notice with the new line is up at about 0.12 s and fades from about 3.0 s; on End week it carries the two lines that matter.
Reduced motion otherwise behaves: no count-up, meters jump, and the week heading, captions, the phone notice and dialogs all still show.

findings.title: Reduced motion hides every change chip: they sit at opacity 0 for their whole 1.7 s
findings.where: src/styles/base.css:20-22 (the global reduced-motion rule) together with src/styles/app.css:66-67 (.delta and @keyframes deltaFloat); the chip is drawn by src/ui/app/Kpis.jsx:13-26 and :38. Present in the release build.
findings.evidence: Release build, prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, Internal politics: the .delta elements 'energy −20' and 'stress +2' are in the page with computed opacity 0, animation deltaFloat, duration 1e-06s; with full motion they are at opacity 1 (picture: test-results/audit/feel/release-politics-reduced-vs-full.png). Test build, signed $40,000 deal: '+$40,000', '+$4,800' and '−28' exist from t=25 ms to t=1725 ms at opacity 0.00 in every frame, and the numbers jump with no count-up (that part is by design), so a reduced-motion player gets no sign of what changed (test-results/audit/feel/reduced-close40k.txt). Cause: the rule shortens every animation to .001 ms, and deltaFloat ends on opacity:0 with fill 'both', so the chip rests on its last keyframe. On a phone it is a visible glitch: app.css:273 hides the 'Closed this quarter' label while a chip is present, so the label blinks out for 1.7 s with nothing in its place (test-results/audit/feel/phone-reduced-vs-full-kpi.png). No browser test looks at .delta.
findings.proposal: One rule next to the chip's own style in app.css: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){ .delta{animation:none} }. The chip then shows, still, until Kpis.jsx removes it at 1.7 s. Same pattern the project already uses at src/styles/claink.css:205 and src/styles/memo.css:35. Tried in my own page only (no file changed): chips at opacity 1.00 from 26 ms to 1710 ms (test-results/audit/feel/reduced-chips-compare.png).
findings.risk: Very low. For reduced-motion players the chip appears and leaves without a fade, which is what they asked for. A reduced-motion check on the chip's opacity in test/e2e would keep it fixed.

findings.title: A signed deal is the quietest line in the log: grey icon, while lost deals are red and warnings amber
findings.where: src/ui/app/Activity.jsx:8 and src/ui/app/LogPeek.jsx:96 (only 'bad' and 'warn' become a class); src/styles/app.css:157 (.line.good .icon{color:var(--good)} is written and nothing emits it); src/game/deals.js:197 (close.signed is logged as 'info').
findings.evidence: test-results/audit/feel/compare-right-4.png, 0.4 s after each press at 1366x768. Signed $40,000: the row leaves the list and a grey handshake line appears, 'Close push: 1 signed. $40,000 is no longer a hypothetical. Commission $4,800.', whose only chip is the cost, '−28 energy'. CRM cleanup: a row leaves the list, grey line, '−15 energy · +6 manager'. No signature: amber icon. Lost deal: red icon. The board after a signing and after a loss is identical ('4 open · $30,000 in pipeline'); only the words and the icon colour separate them, and the win is the one with no colour. test-results/audit/feel/signed-among-warns.png: a Hail Mary that signs $40,000 is the grey line between two amber ones; on a Friday the clAInk invoice (−$293) is amber and 'Friday closes: 1 signed, $40,000 closed' is grey and last in its batch. On a phone with the stat cards scrolled away (where Close deals is pressed) the green chips and the count-up are off screen and the strip's cash goes $900 to $5,700 with no chip: the grey notice is the whole feedback (test-results/audit/feel/phone-compare-close-vs-crm.png). With clAInk's workspace open and tall, a Friday signing line starts below the fold (test-results/audit/feel/friday-close-ck-tall-f03.png).
findings.proposal: Give the two signing tags (close.signed and ck.signed, the CLOSE_TAGS of src/engine/audio/tagmap.js:51) the class 'good' where a line's class is chosen: one small helper in src/ui/app/logLook.js used by Activity.jsx:8 and LogPeek.jsx:96, so the rule already at app.css:157 paints the handshake green in the log and in the phone notice. No motion, no new colour, no engine or save change (the stored kind stays 'info'). Tried in my own page only: test-results/audit/feel/try-good-crop.png.
findings.risk: Low. The log's colour vocabulary gains its third, already-styled member; QA pictures of a log with a signing change by one icon colour. It does not help a line that is below the fold, and there is no small fix for that which keeps the tested rule that the one-screen layout shows no notice (test/e2e/resilience.cjs, section 7).

findings.title: The announcer marks CRM cleanup every time and a $40,000 signing never (the line is drawn at $45,000)
findings.where: src/engine/audio/tagmap.js:18 (act.crm plays 'crm' and the PA line 'hygiene') and :53 (BIG_CLOSE = 45000); src/engine/audio/director.js:18; lines in src/copy/pa.js:44 and :46.
findings.evidence: Same state, 1366x768, sound and announcer on (the defaults). CRM cleanup: crm sound at 10 ms, PA chime at 11 ms, caption 'Pipeline hygiene is everyone's responsibility.' in the top bar from 27 ms until past 3.6 s, spoken at 731 ms (test-results/audit/feel/crm.txt). Signed $40,000 deal: the cash sound at 11 ms and nothing else; the top bar is empty in all 14 frames (test-results/audit/feel/close40k.txt). $44,999: cash only. $50,000: cash plus 'Large sale verified. Ring something.' Picture of the three top bars: test-results/audit/feel/topbar-close-vs-crm.png. With sound off the CRM caption still appears. On a phone that is two notices for CRM (the line and the PA caption) against one for the signing (test-results/audit/feel/phone-compare-close-vs-crm.png). CRM cleanup is the only routine action with an announcer line on every use; the brief's own example amount sits $5,000 under the threshold. I found no reason on file for 45,000 (CHANGELOG, QA report and copydeck searched).
findings.proposal: BIG_CLOSE = 40000 in tagmap.js:53: a quarter of quota, and still above any ordinary single deal (at most $31,200 for a lead and $37,700 for a middling referral, at reputation 100). The existing line, chime and caption do the rest. Update the hand-written label 'close.signed >= 45000' in test/audio/behaviour.test.mjs:24 and test/audio/golden/routing.json:414. Leave the hygiene line alone: it is the joke.
findings.risk: Low. 'Large sale verified' is heard a little more often (its bank has one line; the 6 s cooldown still applies) and on a Friday it outranks the week's own line, as it already does at $45,000. The golden routing file is keyed by a label, not by the constant, so the suite stays green even if the label is left stale.

findings.title: clAInk's staged strike report is given away about two seconds early by the log, the phone notice and the change chips
findings.where: src/ui/ClainkUi.jsx:381-408 (the beats; :442-445 holds the strike box back on purpose); src/ui/app/Activity.jsx (shows the run's lines at once); src/ui/app/LogPeek.jsx:59 (raises them at about 0.1 s); src/ui/app/Kpis.jsx:13-26 (chips at once). Intent on file: CHANGELOG.md:242, 'The strike box fills when the strike card lands ... not while the agents are still "working"'.
findings.evidence: Fixture ck-active-1-strike, Run agents, 1366x768 (test-results/audit/feel/ckstrike-sheet-right.png): at t=21 ms the Activity log, directly above the workspace, already reads 'Strike 2/3 (Procurement): Attempted to purchase itself a seat.' while the workspace says 'Agents orchestrating… 266K tokens' with one box filled; the card, the stamp, the PA line and the second box arrive at t=2082 ms. Strike with real damage (test-results/audit/feel/ckhurt.txt): chips '−$6,600' and '−$792' show from 34 ms and are gone at 1723 ms; the card that explains them lands at 2073 ms. Strike 3 (test-results/audit/feel/ckrevoke-sheet.png): at 22 ms the log reads 'Third strike. Seat revoked. Final true-up: $6,331 charged.', the deal has left the list and cash is counting down under a '−$6,331' chip that has faded by 1.72 s; the Strike 3 card, the blue-screen sound and HR's line come at 2.07 s. On a phone (test-results/audit/feel/phone-ckstrike-sheet-all.png) the notice at the bottom announces 'Strike 2/3 …' at 104 ms, stays about 3.5 s and covers the 'Closed: $0' beat and part of the strike card as they land. The sound side is already held back for exactly this reason (src/engine/audio/tagmap.js:55-58, RUN_TAGS).
findings.proposal: Treat the run's lines on screen the way the sound director already treats them. Smallest first: (a) LogPeek.jsx:59, do not raise RUN_TAGS lines: the workspace the player just pressed is showing them. (b) Activity: add a run's lines when its report has had its say. The page already hears the start and the end (onReport(false) and onReport(true), src/ui/Game.jsx:239, ClainkUi.jsx:534-535) and can hand the board a 'hold the run's lines' flag between the two. With reduced motion or a minimized workspace the report ends at once, so nothing is held. Optional, same flag: let the chips wait too (the hold in the Friday-dialog finding).
findings.risk: (a) alone is low risk and fixes the phone. (b) is medium: the parity driver reads the log from the page (test/parity/drivers/next.cjs:199) and test/e2e/resilience.cjs:115 presses .claink-deploy and looks 300 ms later; the flag must always be cleared when a report is skipped, the workspace unmounts (New run, Load) or a deploy is refused. Screen readers lose nothing: the workspace's own live region speaks the result at once.

findings.title: Reaching quota is not marked: at 106% the meter is the same grey bar and the moment is an ordinary close
findings.where: src/ui/app/Kpis.jsx:64-65 (the quota meter never takes a kind); src/styles/app.css:63-64.
findings.evidence: State at $130,000 (81%) with a $40,000 deal, signed (test-results/audit/feel/quota-sheet-kpi2.png, timeline test-results/audit/feel/quota.txt): exactly the feedback of any signing (cash sound, '+$40,000' and '+$4,800' chips, count-up to $170,000, meter 81.2% to 100% in 150 ms) and then a full grey bar, '106%' and '49 percentage points ahead of pace'. No line, no announcer, nothing that says the number the whole game is about has been reached. Energy and stress meters use green, amber and red; the quota meter is --text-2 at every length. The copydeck has no line for this moment, so I propose no words.
findings.proposal: Kpis.jsx:65: className={"meter" + (p.done >= 1 ? " good" : "")}, which is the existing .meter.good green at exactly the QBR's Club line (src/game/quarter.js:14, club: 1). A state, not an effect: no motion, no sound, no copy. Tried in my own page only: test-results/audit/feel/try-good-crop.png.
findings.risk: Low. It returns to grey if clAInk claws revenue back under 100%, which is truthful. QA pictures of at-quota states change. A sound for the moment would need a new trigger outside the log director; not recommended in this pass.

findings.title: On a Friday with a choice, the week's change chips play dimmed under the dialog and are gone before it is answered
findings.where: src/ui/app/Kpis.jsx:13-26 (useDelta starts at once and lasts 1.7 s), against src/ui/app/LogPeek.jsx:20-22 and :38-39 (the notice waits for the dialog) and test/e2e/phone.cjs:121 ('while an event's choice is open no notice sits dimmed under it').
findings.evidence: End week into the pricing dialog at 1366x768 (test-results/audit/feel/friday-dialog-f02.png, timeline test-results/audit/feel/friday-dialog.txt): the dialog is open at 27 ms; chips '+15', '−4' and '+$1,000' appear at 46 ms under the 72% backdrop and are removed at 1729 ms, while the dialog has two options to read. After the answer the dashboard shows new numbers and no chips. A Friday signing would lose its '+$40,000' the same way. The team already holds the phone notice back for this case and tests it; the chips are not held.
findings.proposal: Give useDelta a hold argument (Kpis passes !!waiting(s), from src/game/run.js): while a choice is waiting keep the baseline and show nothing; once it is answered show one chip for the whole change, Friday's and the choice's together. About four lines in Kpis.jsx.
findings.risk: Low to medium. Chip timing changes in weeks with a dialog, and for clAInk's manager acknowledgement (which waits for the report). The count-up is not held, so the number still moves under the dialog. If judged marginal, leaving it is defensible: the log lists everything Friday did.

findings.title: A stage change is applied in one frame with no mark on the rows that moved
findings.where: src/ui/app/Deals.jsx:18-20; the reusable keyframe is at src/styles/app.css:48-49 (weekIn).
findings.evidence: Discovery with three leads, all qualified (test-results/audit/feel/discovery-sheet-rightx3.png, timeline test-results/audit/feel/discovery.txt): at t=15 ms three rows change 'Lead' to 'Qualified' (pips 1 to 2), one row jumps a place in the sort and one mood changes; no animation ran on any deal row (the only ones running were the energy chip, the meter widths and the button's hover transition). Readable on a six-row board. On the 24-deal board the rows that moved are below the fold and nothing in the visible list changes at all; the count badges and the log line carry it (test-results/audit/feel/board24-discovery-sheet-right.png).
findings.proposal: If anything: key={d.stage} and the existing week-in class on the stage cell (Deals.jsx:20), so the 0.32 s fade-and-rise already used for the week heading replays on the pips and stage name of exactly the rows that moved, and on new rows. Reduced motion gets none of it through the global rule.
findings.risk: Low, but every stage cell also plays it once whenever the list is first drawn (load, new run), and the layout and matrix suites measure boxes that would carry a 4 px transform for 0.32 s. Little value on long boards. Leaving it alone is reasonable.

not_checked: What it sounds like. Headless Chromium has no audible output: I recorded which presets the engine started and when (its own onPlay hook), which lines it handed to the speech engine, and read the synthesis parameters. Loudness, mix and the voice were not heard.

Browsers other than Chromium (the only one installed) and real phones: touch feel, tap highlight, speech voices. The reduced-motion defect rests on standard CSS behaviour but was only seen in Chromium.
The other five endings and their cutscenes; the security-incident dialog and Friday events other than the pricing dialog; QBR lines of a run that continues.

The proposals. Three were tried as run-time CSS in my own page only (the reduced-motion rule, the green icon, the green meter). Nothing was built and no suite was run, so their effect on test/e2e (layout, matrix, phone, resilience), the parity harness and the audio routing golden file is unverified.

Timing precision: on-screen times come from requestAnimationFrame sampling (16 ms steps) in headless Chromium at 1366x768 and 390x844; each screenshot's time is the middle of a 30–80 ms window. Tools and all timelines are in test-results/audit/feel/ (seq.cjs, rapid.cjs, sheet.sh, one .txt per sequence).
How often the announcer's cooldown or a busy speech engine swallows the CRM line in real play. It fired in every run I made, but each was a fresh page.
